geos.label: South Bay
geos.blurb: San Jose, Saratoga, Sunnyvale, Mountain View

meta.standfirst: Arts, music, and worthwhile oddities, ordered by remove from Mountain View.

events.title: OMEGA X
events.note: K-pop boy group whose members left their original label in a public labour dispute and rebuilt as an independent act — the touring underdog story is most of the draw. A 500-seat civic theatre is an unusually small room for this. Found on a ticketing feed only; confirm the time before you go.

events.title: Kamasi Washington
events.note: Closing night of a two-night run, and the week's single best argument for leaving the house. Washington plays big-band spiritual jazz in the Pharoah Sanders line — choir, two drummers, horns stacked like weather. Yoshi's holds 400, which is a quarter of the room he normally fills. Two sets, 7:30 and 9:30.

events.title: The Spits, The Fleshies, The Pranks
events.note: Night one of two. Seattle-via-Michigan cretin punk: two-chord songs, cheap keyboards, masks. They have made the same record for twenty-five years and it keeps working. Doors 8, music 9. Bottom of the Hill has announced it closes at the end of 2026, so the room itself is now part of the reason to go.

events.title: The Tear Garden, Anthony Xavier Jackson
events.note: Edward Ka-Spel of the Legendary Pink Dots and cEvin Key of Skinny Puppy, a forty-year side project that has outlasted most people's main ones. Slow, narcotic psychedelia with industrial bones. They tour rarely enough that this is a genuine event for anyone who cares.

events.title: Haute & Freddy
events.note: Sold out, and moved here from Bimbo's — the Castro's box office lists it without a genre line and I could not find a reliable description of the act, so this one is a name on a marquee. Doors 7. If you already have a ticket you know more than I do.

events.title: Letty Lynton
events.note: Part of Wild, Weird, Wicked: Films from Before the Code. The 1932 Joan Crawford melodrama that lost a plagiarism suit and was pulled from circulation for most of a century — you effectively cannot stream it, which is the whole point of a repertory house.

events.title: Freeway
events.note: Arthouse 50. Matthew Bright's 1996 Little Red Riding Hood retelling with Reese Witherspoon and Kiefer Sutherland, a film so tonally deranged it took twenty years to be taken seriously. Pairs badly and therefore well with the pre-Code bill upstairs.

events.title: Cyberpunk Cinema Night
events.note: Free projection night in a Mission dive, programmed around neon and bad futures. The kind of thing that never reaches a listings platform and is exactly why a Monday is not automatically dead.

events.title: Motown on Mondays
events.note: A standing Monday, running well over a decade: all-45s soul and Motown, free before 8pm and $5 after. Listed once rather than every week. Madrone is small and it fills.

events.title: Death Guild
events.note: The longest continuously running goth-industrial night in the United States, every Monday since 1993. 18+. Monday Night Hubba runs in the smaller room the same evening. Listed once for the window rather than weekly.

events.title: Japanese Tea Garden free admission hour
events.venue: Japanese Tea Garden, Golden Gate Park
events.note: Standing arrangement, not a one-off: the first hour is free every Monday, Wednesday and Friday, $12–$16 otherwise. Listed once here rather than three times. At nine o'clock it is genuinely empty.

events.title: Alphabet Soup
events.note: Long-running Bay Area live hip-hop band — freestyle over a real rhythm section rather than over a laptop. A 150-cap room on San Pablo Ave; a Monday booking like this is the Ivy Room's whole character.

events.title: Beyond the Bridge: film and conversation on homelessness
events.venue: Screening with panel, downtown San Francisco
events.note: Documentary plus panel on housing policy, free with RSVP. The aggregator did not name the venue and I could not confirm it — RSVP first and get the address from the confirmation rather than turning up somewhere.

events.title: Gregory Alan Isakov with the San Francisco Symphony
events.note: A one-off: Isakov's spare Colorado folk songs given full symphonic arrangements. Songs this quiet usually lose in a 2,700-seat hall, so the orchestration is the experiment. Pricey on the resale market. Davies sits behind a ticketing queue and could not be polled directly; the date is confirmed from three independent sellers.

events.title: Squeeze, Adam Ant, Haircut 100
events.note: Three 1979–82 British singles bands on one bill. Squeeze are the reason to come — Difford and Tilbrook wrote some of the sharpest pop lyrics of the era and still sing them in key. Adam Ant remains a genuinely strange stage presence. Starts early at 7.

events.title: Starbomb with Epic Rap Battles of History
events.note: Video-game parody rap from the Game Grumps orbit, touring with the Epic Rap Battles of History cast. Not a music recommendation so much as a large, affectionate internet reunion. All ages, doors 7, show 8.

events.title: Jeff Bernat: Luv Language Tour
events.note: Smooth bedroom R&B that found its audience through streaming rather than radio — a Korean-American singer with a far bigger following in Seoul and Manila than in the city he is playing. Doors 7.

events.title: Magic Sword, Skylimit
events.note: MOVED: this was billed at The Chapel and is now at Kilowatt, a much smaller Mission bar. Masked synthwave with a comic-book mythology attached — heavy arpeggios, no vocals. Doors 6, show 7. Check your ticket says Kilowatt.

events.title: The Spits, The Fleshies, Garras Sucias
events.note: Night two, different support: Garras Sucias replace The Pranks. If you are choosing one, take tonight — the Oakland hardcore opener is the better of the two undercards.

events.title: El Grito de Independencia
events.note: The cry of independence, called at the hour it is called in Mexico City, with mariachi, ballet folklórico and food stalls beforehand. Free, outdoors and the most genuinely civic thing happening this week. Dress for a Civic Center evening — the plaza funnels wind.

events.title: Civic Center Soundtrack: free concerts and food trucks
events.note: Runs Tuesdays and Thursdays through the season; listed once for the window. Lunchtime bands on the Fulton Street plaza between the library and City Hall, with trucks. Modest, but it is free live music in the middle of a working day.

events.title: John Pizzarelli: Dear Mr. Bennett
events.note: Two nights, Tuesday and Wednesday. A seven-string guitarist and crooner doing a Tony Bennett tribute programme — swing played straight, no irony, considerable technique. The kind of booking Yoshi's does better than anywhere else within fifty miles.

events.title: Johnny Blue Skies & The Dark Clouds
events.note: Sturgill Simpson under the name he now records as, playing outdoors in the Berkeley hills. SOLD OUT. Doors 5:30, show 7 — early, because the Greek has a hard curfew. It gets cold up there after dark regardless of the afternoon.

events.title: The Obsessed
events.note: Wino's band, one of the foundational American doom acts, in a 150-capacity room. Slow, loud, blues-derived riffs played by people who were doing this before the genre had a name. An absurdly small room for it.

events.title: No Right, withpaperwings and more
events.note: Five dollars, all ages, volunteer-run, no bar. Gilman's economics have not moved in thirty years and neither has its door policy. Hardcore bill, 6:30 start — it is over early enough to get back across the bridge.

events.title: $6 Tuesday at the Solano Drive-In
events.note: One of the last operating drive-ins in the Bay Area, and Tuesdays are six dollars for a double feature. Sound is over FM, so bring a car with a working radio and something warm. Listed once for the window; it runs weekly.

events.title: Five Finger Death Punch, Cody Jinks, Eva Under Fire
events.note: A mainstream metal package with an outlaw-country singer bolted onto it, which tells you where both audiences now overlap. Cheap on the lawn. Shoreline parking is $40 and the bike path from central Mountain View is genuinely faster.

events.title: Santana Row Farmers' Market
events.note: Twenty-five growers and makers on the Row every Wednesday afternoon through the end of September, so this is one of the last. Note that the Tuesday Sips & Sounds concert series that ran here through August appears to have finished — I could find no September dates.

events.title: The Infamous Stringdusters, Silas Herman
events.note: Grammy-winning progressive bluegrass — traditional instrumentation pushed into jam-band lengths and jazz harmony. The Guild is a beautifully restored 500-seat room four minutes' walk from Caltrain Menlo Park, which beats parking on Santa Cruz Ave. Doors 6:30.

events.title: Curating America's 250th
events.note: Museum professionals on how you mount a semiquincentennial exhibition without producing either pageantry or a lecture. Free, with a suggested $15 that members skip. A small, serious evening in a town that rarely gets one.

events.title: Chelsea Wolfe, Jonathan Hultén
events.note: THE DARK World Tour. Wolfe writes gothic folk that keeps drifting into metal weight — close-miked voice over sub-bass and distortion. Hultén, formerly of Tribulation, opens solo and acoustic. A seated Broadway house is an odd, probably excellent, fit for this. 8:30 start.

events.title: When Chai Met Toast
events.note: Kerala four-piece singing in Malayalam, Hindi and English over banjo and folk-pop arrangements — cheerful, unfashionable and very good at it. SOLD OUT. Doors 7.

events.title: ALI, The Helltones
events.note: Doors 7, show 8. Rickshaw is a converted TV studio with a balcony, which means good sightlines from everywhere and a bar you can actually reach. Local support from The Helltones.

events.title: Unity record release, Quaaludes, Yeoubi
events.note: A record release on a Wednesday for thirteen dollars, with two of the better Bay Area punk bands under it. This is the cheapest good show of the week by a distance.

events.title: Zee Machine, boy bowser
events.note: Synth-pop with a queer confessional streak, in the basement room under the Swedish American Hall. Du Nord is a low-ceilinged former speakeasy and sounds like one — good for this, bad for anything with cymbals.

events.title: The American Astronaut (35mm)
events.note: Twenty-fifth anniversary, on actual 35mm. Cory McAbee's black-and-white space-western musical, made for almost nothing, and unlike anything before or since. Prints of this barely exist; it is the screening of the week for anyone who cares about format.

events.title: American Doctor
events.note: Co-presented by the Arab Film & Media Institute and the Jewish Film Institute — two organisations that do not routinely share a bill, which is itself the news here.

events.title: Art Battle San Francisco
events.note: Competitive live painting: twelve artists, twenty minutes a round, the audience votes. Absurd as a format and consistently entertaining as an evening. Public Works is a warehouse room, so there is space to circulate around the easels.

events.title: People in Plazas: Emily Day Swingtet
events.note: Small-group swing in a downtown privately-owned public space at lunchtime — the People in Plazas series has been quietly doing this since the 1970s. A soul and funk set runs the same hour at 555 California if you would rather have horns.

events.title: Inside the 2026 SF Ballot: live Q&A with journalists
events.note: Local reporters taking questions on the measures, six weeks out from the election. Free, in the library basement, and considerably more useful than the voter guide.

events.title: Old Blind Dogs
events.note: Scottish trad, thirty-five years in: fiddle and pipes over a percussion approach borrowed from West Africa, which is less of a gimmick than it sounds. The Freight is a seated listening room, not a club — people actually shut up.

events.title: Barbara Forever
events.note: Alternative Visions, BAMPFA's experimental strand. Brydie O'Connor's Teddy Award winner, which also plays the Roxie on Friday with the director present — if you want the Q&A, take the Friday.

events.title: Christian Molenaar, Adam Lion, Mike Meanstreetz, Kevin Murray
events.note: Four-set noise and free-improv bill in an Oakland warehouse space. This is the part of the scene that no calendar aggregates properly; time and door price were not published, so check the space's socials on the day.

events.title: Patti Smith: Songs & Stories
events.note: City Arts & Lectures, with Tony Shanahan and her son Jackson Smith playing. She is here for the new memoir, Bread of Angels, but a Patti Smith reading has never stayed a reading — it turns into a set. Some tickets include the book. The single best thing on Thursday.

events.title: Mustard Service, Pity Party (Girls Club), Manwolves, Chicano Mosh
events.note: Miami indie with a bossa-nova lilt, on a four-band bill that leans Latinx across the board. Good value for a Thursday — the undercard is the interesting half.

events.title: Unsane, CNTS, Facet
events.note: New York noise rock at its most punishing — detuned, metallic, built on Chris Spencer's shout. Thirty-five years of it and no softening. Loud enough that earplugs are not a suggestion.

events.title: American Aquarium, Buffalo Nichols
events.note: The support is the story: Buffalo Nichols plays spare, modern country blues that refuses the genre's usual nostalgia. American Aquarium do hard-bitten alt-country above him. Best pound-for-pound bill of the night.

events.title: Dutch Melrose, Benny Mayne, Pretty Havoc
events.note: Doors 7, show 8. A 300-cap room on Mission at Duboce with a sound system better than the room deserves.

events.title: Boys Go To Jupiter, Abby Kenna
events.note: Bedroom indie moved onto a stage. Upstairs the same night, Big Brain Lectures takes over the Swedish American Hall — nerd-adjacent talks, different door.

events.title: Cantonese Opera Festival with costume try-ons
events.note: Free with RSVP. Performances plus the chance to be dressed in full Cantonese opera costume and painted — the try-on is the part people queue for. An art form with a deep local history and a shrinking number of public showings.

events.title: Opening night: Protest Photography Through the Decades
events.note: Exhibition opening drawn from the library's own photographic holdings. Free, and the archive is stronger on Bay Area protest than any museum collection in the city.

events.title: Big Art Loop: Waterfront Walkabout
events.note: A free guided stroll of the public art along the Embarcadero, ending at the Exploratorium. Two miles, flat, and the light on the bay at six is the actual argument. RSVP recommended, not required.

events.title: Out of Character: readings and an art talk
events.note: Free literary night in the Dogpatch gallery complex, pairing readings with a talk from an exhibiting artist. Minnesota Street Project is a dozen galleries under one roof, so come early and walk the building first.

events.title: CritterFest film festival
events.note: A new festival of short films about pets and animals in the Richmond's restored 4-Star. Exactly the sort of cheerfully narrow programming a neighbourhood cinema should be doing. The $5 EBT rate is worth stating.

events.title: NightLife at the California Academy of Sciences
events.note: The 21+ Thursday opening: rainforest dome, aquarium and planetarium with a bar and DJs, minus the school groups. $26, or $5 on an EBT card. Last entry 9pm — people miss the planetarium by arriving at 8:45.

events.title: Fort Mason Art Walk, with Leah Rosenberg's The Sea Is But Another Sky
events.note: The autumn walk across Fort Mason's galleries, timed to the unveiling of a new Rosenberg wall work — she paints in stacked bands of colour, and the pier setting gives her a horizon to argue with. Haines Gallery's 250 Years, Indigenous Futures is also newly up on the campus.

events.title: Yoon Chung Han: Dreaming Babies: illi (opening)
events.note: Opens today and runs to 22 October. Data-driven installation work in Gray Area's Mission theatre — the one venue in the city that reliably shows audiovisual and machine-made art as art rather than as demo. A workshop on community assemblies for AI runs the same day.

events.title: Echo by RAWdance
events.note: Contemporary dance in a small Montgomery Street art space — RAWdance's work is built around duets and close contact, which suits a room this size. Price was not published; the listing came from the downtown business association rather than the company.

events.title: The Presidio's 250th birthday
events.note: Two hundred and fifty years since the Spanish garrison was founded on this ground in 1776 — older than the United States by two months. Free with RSVP.

events.title: Bleachers, The Linda Lindas
events.note: Jack Antonoff's band, with the far more interesting opener: The Linda Lindas are now several years past the viral library video and have turned into a genuinely good punk band. Doors 5, show 6:30. Layers — the Greek gets cold.

events.title: The Bald and the Beautiful LIVE: Very Bald, Very Beautiful
events.note: Trixie Mattel and Katya taking their podcast on stage in a 3,000-seat Art Deco cathedral — the Paramount's 1931 interior is worth the ticket on its own. Downtown Oakland garages mostly close their gates at 7pm; take BART to 19th St.

events.title: Tony Lindsay, Nona Brown, Bryan Dyer
events.note: Lindsay sang lead with Santana for two decades and holds several Grammys for it; here he is fronting a straight soul revue with two strong Bay Area vocalists beside him. Seated room, which for once suits the material.

events.title: Scissoring, Gwyniever, Lilotus
events.note: Queer punk bill in a 150-cap Telegraph Ave dive with red flocked wallpaper and no pretensions. Three local bands, cheap door, over by midnight.

events.title: Rolling Quartz
events.note: Korean all-woman hard rock band, five-piece, playing actual instruments loudly — a rarity in a K-market built around choreography. Found on a ticketing feed; CryBaby publishes little, so confirm the door time.

events.title: OakTown Thursdays
events.note: Free street programming on the pedestrianised block at Telegraph and Broadway — vendors, DJs, food. Downtown Oakland's evening foot traffic has been the city's hard problem for years and this is the deliberate answer to it. BART 12th St, one minute.

events.title: Phantom Planet, Arkells
events.note: Yes, that Phantom Planet — but the band reformed and the recent records are better than the one song everybody remembers. Arkells are a big Canadian rock act playing a 500-seat room, which is the anomaly worth noticing. Doors 7.

events.title: Mark Karan's Budz
events.note: Karan played guitar in Bob Weir's RatDog and The Other Ones for years; this is his own band working the same Dead-adjacent territory. Doors 7:30. Club Fox is three minutes from Caltrain Redwood City.

events.title: Beats, Brews & Vines
events.note: Third Thursday of the month, August to October, so this is the middle one. Broadway closes, a band plays, there is beer and wine for sale. Small-town Peninsula programming done properly. BART and Caltrain both stop at Millbrae.

events.title: Casey Gerald: The Great Refusal
events.note: Gerald's first book, There Will Be No Miracles Here, was a memoir that refused every redemption arc available to it. The new one argues for refusal as a political position. Kepler's events sell out at this scale — book ahead.

events.title: The Temptations and The Four Tops
events.note: Two Motown institutions on a hillside above Saratoga at sunset. Neither has an original lead singer left, which is the honest caveat — but the arrangements and the harmony discipline are the real inheritance, and both groups keep them. $20 parking with a shuttle up the hill.

events.title: Constitution Day community conversation
events.note: Free with RSVP, on the anniversary of the signing. The aggregator did not name the room — most likely the library or the community center; RSVP and take the address from the confirmation.

events.title: Dianne Reeves with Branford Marsalis
events.note: Two nights, Friday and Saturday. Five Grammys, the most complete jazz voice working, and Branford Marsalis beside her rather than behind her — this is a duo-weighted billing, not a singer with a band. The fall season's real opening statement. Muni Van Ness, four minutes; the garage is $40.

events.title: San Francisco Greek Festival
events.note: Runs Friday and Saturday 11am–10pm and Sunday noon–7pm, on the cathedral's hilltop above the Mission. Free to enter. Dance troupes on the hour, a taverna that serves until late, and the pastry table that empties first. Listed once for the three days.

events.title: Oktoberfest on Front
events.venue: Front Street Entertainment Zone, at Schroeder's
events.note: Free with RSVP. The street outside Schroeder's — a German restaurant on that block since 1893 — closes for a block party with a brass band. One of the Financial District's new open-container entertainment zones, which is why the beer is allowed on the pavement.

events.title: Union Square Dances
events.note: Free outdoor social dancing in the middle of the square on a Friday evening — lesson first, then the floor opens. No partner needed and no one is watching you as closely as you think.

events.title: Off the Grid: Fort Mason Friday Night Market
events.note: Thirty-odd trucks on the Fort Mason parking lot with the Golden Gate behind them. The season's end is close, so take a Friday while the light lasts. Free to enter; bring a jacket, the wind comes straight off the bay.

events.title: From the E: Excelsior Latino Heritage Night Market
events.note: The Excelsior's own night market, this edition built around Latino Heritage Month. All ages, free, and a long way from the tourist-facing versions of this format downtown.

events.title: Free Coffee Concert
events.note: Chamber music at ten in the morning under the glass atrium of a Financial District bank hall, free, with coffee. A genuinely lovely and almost unattended hour.

events.title: Daniel Avery (live), Draag
events.note: Live, not a DJ set — Avery builds long, corroded techno arcs out of hardware, closer to shoegaze than to a club. 9pm start. The Independent's floor is one of the better places in the city to stand still for ninety minutes.

events.title: Citizen, Hotline TNT, Anxious, Cryogeyser
events.note: A four-band emo and fuzz-pop package where the support is unusually strong — Hotline TNT's blown-out melodic guitar is the reason to arrive early. 1,400-cap ballroom with a balcony.

events.title: The Exploited, Total Chaos, Dwarves
events.note: Scottish street punk from 1979, still led by Wattie Buchan, with San Francisco's own Dwarves third on the bill — a band who have been genuinely disreputable for forty years. A rough, loud, very old-school night off Union Square.

events.title: Lido Pimienta, Chancha Via Circuito
events.note: The best-matched double bill of the week. Pimienta sings Afro-Colombian song forms through art-pop production; Chancha Via Circuito built digital cumbia into something slow and hallucinatory. In Bimbo's 1931 supper-club room, this should be extraordinary. Doors 7, 21+.

events.title: Shawn James, Gravedancer
events.note: Big-voiced dark Americana, heavier and more theatrical than the acoustic guitar suggests. The Chapel is a former mortuary with a 40-foot arched ceiling, which flatters exactly this. Doors 8.

events.title: Sweeping Promises, Fake Fruit, System Exclusive
events.note: Taut, treble-forward post-punk recorded in a single room on one mic, and it translates live better than that method has any right to. Oakland's Fake Fruit are a strong middle slot. Best small-room bill on Friday.

events.title: Steel Pole Bath Tub, Ovarian Trolley, Wife
events.note: A reunion of the Bay Area's own noise-rock institution, with Ovarian Trolley — mid-90s Bay riot-adjacent art punk — beneath them. Effectively a wake for a scene, in the room that housed it, in the year that room closes. Doors 7:30.

events.title: BIIRD (night 1)
events.note: SOLD OUT, all ages, with a second night on Sunday that still had tickets at the time of writing. Doors 8.

events.title: RUSSELL!, Nari, Darilø
events.note: Three-act local pop bill in the basement. A ticketing feed also lists Russell Thompkins Jr. of The Stylistics in the building the same night, presumably upstairs in the Swedish American Hall — I could not confirm that against the venue, so treat it as unverified rather than as a soul show you can count on.

events.title: Âme (Innervisions), Rodriguez Jr.
events.note: Deep, melodic Berlin house from the label that defined the sound for a decade. Public Works' main room is wooden and warm and the sound system is the best argument for the venue. A long night — this is not an 11pm-and-home booking.

events.title: Mild Minds, edapollo
events.note: Melodic Australian house on 1015's main floor. The venue's own site fetched empty this week, so the date comes from a ticketing feed — worth a check before you commit to a 1am taxi.

events.title: K Motionz
events.note: UK drum and bass in the Dogpatch warehouse. The Midway is one of the few rooms in the city with the ceiling height and the rig for this. $20 lot parking, or the T from downtown.

events.title: Latin Throwbacks: 90s and 2000s
events.note: Reggaetón, bachata and merengue from the two decades that built the format, 18+. DNA runs two rooms, so the bill on the small stage may differ from the flyer.

events.title: Movies at Mechanics' Presents
events.note: The 1854 Mechanics' Institute — spiral-staircase library, chess room upstairs — runs a small film night in its meeting hall. Worth going for the building alone. Title and price were not published in the listing I could reach.

events.title: Jack Harlow, James Savage
events.note: Rescheduled from 21 September, and he plays The Masonic in the city on Saturday — the Fox is the better room by a wide margin, with its gilded plaster and 2,800 seats. Doors 7. BART 19th St, two minutes; do not park on the street here.

events.title: Alice Gerrard, Justin Robinson, Forty Drop Few
events.note: Gerrard is ninety-two and is the reason there were women singing lead in bluegrass at all — Hazel & Alice, 1965, on Folkways. Justin Robinson of the Carolina Chocolate Drops plays with her. There is no guarantee of another chance at this one, and the Freight is a listening room that will do it justice.

events.title: Jazz Is Dead: Cortex, with Adrian Younge and J Rocc
events.note: SOLD OUT. Cortex are the French jazz-funk group whose 1975 record became one of the most sampled in hip-hop; Adrian Younge's Jazz Is Dead label brought them back. J Rocc DJs. Doors 7.

events.title: Big Daddy Kane
events.note: One of the two or three most technically gifted rappers of the late 1980s, and he still performs with a live band rather than to a backing track. A 400-seat jazz club is a strange and rather wonderful place to see him.

events.title: SHE'S, Clean Girl and the Dirty Dishes, The Vaxxines
events.note: Japanese three-piece SHE'S touring a 150-cap Oakland dive, with two sharp local openers under them. This is the sort of booking the Stork Club does that nothing else in the East Bay does.

events.title: Matt Braunger
events.note: Long-form storytelling stand-up in the back room of a Shattuck beer hall — closer to a club set than a theatre show, and better for it. 7pm.

events.title: SEWN, Smashed Teeth, 40 Oz Felony, Cuchillos, I Forgot
events.note: Five bands for five dollars. Gilman remains the cheapest live music per minute anywhere in the region, and the all-ages, no-alcohol policy means the crowd is the young one everyone else claims to want.

events.title: Friday Nights at OMCA: Kiyomi and Cal Raijin Taiko
events.note: Free outdoor programming in the museum gardens with Off the Grid trucks, and taiko in a concrete courtyard is the right acoustic accident. BeHere / 1942, the museum's new show on Japanese American incarceration, opens to the public this weekend. BART Lake Merritt, two minutes.

events.title: Still Ruins, Tube Alloys, Shop Regulars, Clarko
events.note: Four-band local bill at the old blues bar on MacArthur, now Oakland's most reliable small punk room. Door time unpublished; Eli's shows usually start around nine.

events.title: Moonalice, Bert's Brew
events.note: Bay Area psychedelic rock with deep Dead and Airplane lineage, and a poster commissioned for every single show since 2007 — the poster archive is genuinely a cultural artefact at this point. Doors 7.

events.title: SONA: 70s and 80s rock covers
events.note: A covers night, listed for completeness rather than championed — the brief is explicit that tribute acts are part of the circuit but never the pick. Doors 7:30. Caltrain Redwood City is three minutes away.

events.title: Nat King Cole Reimagined, with Bill Cunliffe
events.note: Two nights, Friday and Saturday. Cunliffe is a Grammy-winning arranger and a serious pianist, and Meyhouse is the closest thing the mid-Peninsula has to a proper jazz supper room. The nearest good jazz to Mountain View this week by a distance.

events.title: Ren Geisick
events.note: A Bay Area jazz singer in a plant shop that turns into a bar at night — a room of about forty people, no cover listed. The kind of listing that justifies the whole exercise. Confirm on the day; small venues change these plans.

events.title: Opera San José: Don Giovanni
events.note: Mozart's Don Giovanni, running to 27 September in a restored 1927 movie palace that is the most beautiful room in the South Bay. It matters more than usual this month: San Francisco Opera's orchestra is on strike and its season opener was cancelled, so this is the only fully staged grand opera on in the region.

events.title: Music in the Park: Common Kings, Sammy Johnson
events.note: Downtown San Jose's long-running park concert series, founded in 1989 as a free event — recent editions have been ticketed and I could not confirm 2026 pricing, so assume a door charge. Pacific-island reggae and soul from Common Kings, outdoors in the plaza, 6pm.

events.title: Carín León
events.note: Arena show, listed for completeness. León is the most interesting figure in regional Mexican music right now — he has pulled the genre toward country and soul without losing the sierreño core. Expensive, and findable without this digest.

events.title: Kany García
events.note: Puerto Rican singer-songwriter with a shelf of Latin Grammys, working in the cantautora tradition rather than the reggaetón one — guitar, voice, and lyrics that carry the weight. A 3,000-seat room suits her.

events.title: San Jose Bike Party
events.venue: Start point announced the week of the ride
events.note: Third Friday, every month, free: a few thousand people ride a themed route through San Jose with sound systems on trailers. Meet 7:30, roll at 8. The start point goes up on the group's socials days beforehand — do not plan around a fixed address.

events.title: San Jose Harvest & Handmade Discovery Fest
events.note: Three days at Almaden Lake, Friday to Sunday, free to enter: makers, growers and food. Listed once for the run. Details came from a listings aggregator rather than an organiser, so hours may shift.

events.title: Yellow Claw
events.note: Dutch trap and bass duo, late start, in the South Bay's main club room. Street parking is free after six and Caltrain Sunnyvale is a six-minute walk — but the last northbound train goes long before this ends.

events.title: Daft Disko
events.note: A Daft Punk tribute night. Listed because The Ritz is the only real small club in downtown San Jose and its calendar is worth knowing; not because a tribute set beats the original records at home.

events.title: Chinatown Autumn Moon Festival
events.note: Thirty-sixth year, both Saturday and Sunday, free, and the largest of the week's festivals: lion dancing, a dumpling-eating contest, a K-pop dance contest and eight blocks of Grant Avenue closed to traffic. Mooncakes sell out by mid-afternoon. Muni 30 or 45 — there is no parking worth attempting.

events.title: Muni Heritage Weekend
events.note: Saturday and Sunday. Streetcars and buses that normally live in a yard come out and carry passengers for free — 1930s Blackpool trams, an open-top 1914 motor coach, the works. Free rides, no ticket, no queue system beyond turning up.

events.title: Flower Piano
events.price: Free for SF residents with ID; $18 adults otherwise
events.note: Eleventh year, running daily 10–20 September, so Sunday is the last day. Twelve grand pianos scattered across 55 acres, 130 scheduled performances and open play on all of them between times. Free with SF residency, $18 otherwise. Listed once for the run; Saturday is the busiest day.

events.title: Secondhand Saturday with Sunset Mercantile
events.note: Sixty-odd vintage dealers and makers in the outer Sunset. Curated rather than a car-boot sale, which means better stock and higher prices than a flea. Free to browse.

events.title: Glen Park Night Market
events.note: A small neighbourhood market on a closed street in the village — local makers, live music, food. Glen Park BART is at the bottom of the hill, which is the easy way in and the hard way home.

events.title: Free Saturday at the de Young and the Legion of Honor
events.venue: de Young Museum, Golden Gate Park
events.note: Permanent collection free to Bay Area residents at both Fine Arts Museums today, with a timed ticket booked in advance — the walk-up queue is not the plan. Special exhibitions are still charged. The Legion's setting above Land's End is the better half of the pairing.

events.title: Trouble in Paradise
events.venue: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts
events.note: Lubitsch's 1932 jewel-thief comedy, the wittiest film about theft ever made, with themed snacks and gallery entry included in the $15. GaHee Park's unsettling figurative paintings are upstairs. YBCA's galleries are free every Wednesday if you would rather not pay.

events.title: Larry Reed: A Life in Light and Shadow
events.note: A portrait of the Bay Area shadow-theatre master who trained in Balinese wayang kulit and spent fifty years building the form here. Followed at 4pm by SF Lost Neon Landscapes: Chinatown, a shorts programme on the neighbourhood's vanished signage — a good pairing, and the Autumn Moon Festival is eight blocks away.

events.title: Kwaidan (4K restoration)
events.note: Kobayashi's 1964 ghost-story anthology, three hours of hand-painted skies and stillness, restored. One of the most beautiful colour films ever made and hopeless on a laptop.

events.title: Cut Chemist
events.note: Jurassic 5's turntablist, and one of the last DJs who genuinely performs rather than plays — multiple decks, records cut live, a set built in front of you. 9pm.

events.title: Geneva Jacuzzi, EX-HEIR, Diesel Dudes
events.note: LA art-pop performed as ritual: masks, props, costume changes, cold synths. Closer to performance art than to a gig and much funnier than that makes it sound. Doors 8.

events.title: Spiritual Cramp, The She's, Judy
events.note: SOLD OUT. San Francisco's own — swaggering, Clash-indebted punk with a frontman who understands that the job is a performance. A hometown sell-out in a room that closes this year.

events.title: Be Your Own Pet, Iguana Death Cult, Fake Dad
events.note: Nashville garage punk who broke up as teenagers in 2008 and reformed as adults with the speed intact. Rotterdam's Iguana Death Cult are a properly unhinged middle band. Doors 8.

events.title: The Matches
events.note: Oakland pop-punk reunion at the Fillmore, which for a band that came up playing Gilman and the Warfield's opening slots is the local victory lap. Free apples and a poster at the door, as ever.

events.title: Arlo Parks, Baird
events.note: Mercury Prize winner writing quiet, exact songs about other people's interior lives — bedroom soul with a poet's diction. A 2,300-seat theatre is a big room for this and she can fill it.

events.title: Steve Aoki, RIOT TEN, High Society
events.note: Large-format EDM in a 7,000-capacity hall. Listed for completeness. The Civic Center garage is $45; BART or Muni to Civic Center is three minutes' walk and obviously correct.

events.title: The Growlers (night 2)
events.note: Second of two nights, having played Santa Cruz on Thursday. Their reverb-soaked 'beach goth' is a better fit for a 1,400-seat movie palace than it has any right to be. Doors 7.

events.title: MGMT (DJ set)
events.note: A DJ set, not a live show — set expectations accordingly. Andrew VanWyngarden and Ben Goldwasser play records, which given their taste in 1970s cosmic pop is a reasonable prospect on its own terms.

events.title: Spin Control USA Jam, and Why 2K
events.note: Two rooms, two crowds: a turntablism and breaking jam downstairs, all ages, and a Y2K-nostalgia dance night upstairs, 18+. One door price is not clear from the calendar — check which room your ticket is for.

events.title: SF Neo-Futurists: The Neodivergent Wrench
events.note: Thirty plays in sixty minutes, order chosen by the audience shouting numbers, script rewritten weekly. The Neo-Futurist form is thirty years old and still the most alive thing in small-scale theatre. Late start, short run time.

events.title: TideFest
events.note: Free outer-Sunset street festival with live music and an art walk along the ocean end of Taraval. Start time was not published. It will be cold and it will probably be foggy; that is the Sunset and nobody there minds.

events.title: Family Day Block Party
events.note: Free with RSVP, on the Bayview waterfront at India Basin — DJs, food and family activities on a shoreline that has just come through a long and contested park rebuild.

events.title: SFJAZZ presents Ravi Coltrane: Coltrane Centennial Celebration
events.note: John Coltrane would have turned a hundred this month, and his son marks it in Berkeley rather than at SFJAZZ's own hall. SOLD OUT, which tells you the city agreed this was the date to be at. Doors 7.

events.title: Mohini Dey
events.note: Two nights, Saturday and Sunday. An Indian bass player who was doing session work at ten and now plays fusion at a speed that is genuinely difficult to follow. Technique as spectacle, and she has the writing to back it.

events.title: Vieux Farka Touré
events.note: Ali Farka Touré's son, playing the Malian desert blues his father defined and then pushing it toward rock. A beer hall on Shattuck is an unglamorous room for a player of this stature — which is the reason to go. 9pm.

events.title: Uranium Club, Good Flying Birds, EraserCUBE
events.note: Minneapolis art-punk — angular, deadpan, faintly hostile, and very funny if you are paying attention. A 150-cap room for a band who could sell four times that.

events.title: Surplus 1980, Pateka, Murder Murder, Strawberry Panic
events.note: Moe Staiano's long-running avant-punk project heading a four-band bill of Bay Area weirdness. Nothing on this lineup sounds like anything else on it, which is the point.

events.title: Oakland Pride Extravaganza
events.note: Queer punk showcase for five dollars. Note that the city's official Oakland Pride moved to August this year, so this is an independent night rather than part of the festival weekend.

events.title: Contempt
events.note: Godard's Early Films. Le Mépris in CinemaScope — Bardot, Fritz Lang playing himself, and Georges Delerue's theme, which is the most beautiful thing in any Godard picture. Tsai Ming-liang's The Hole follows at 7.

events.title: Lafayette Art & Wine Festival
events.note: Saturday and Sunday, free to enter, several hundred artist booths and four music stages along Mount Diablo Boulevard. Lafayette is beyond the brief's named East Bay towns; filed here as the nearest region. BART Lafayette drops you at the edge of it.

events.title: The Wardrobe Project Flea
events.note: Vintage and secondhand clothing under the BART tracks on College Avenue. Free, outdoors, and the transit answer is in the name.

events.title: Native Boogie and Beats
events.note: Free with RSVP: Indigenous music and dance in an Alameda park, two hours in the middle of the day. Small, and the sort of programming that vanishes from the record if nobody lists it.

events.title: Science@Cal lecture
events.note: Berkeley's monthly free public science lecture, aimed at people who are curious rather than trained. Saturday morning, no ticket, and the campus is pleasant to walk afterwards.

events.title: EBPCO Fest: Bay Area Photo Night
events.note: Photographers' gathering and raffle in an Oakland studio — a scene night rather than a show, which is its own kind of useful if you shoot. Door price was not published.

events.title: Brandi Carlile, CMAT
events.note: The biggest booking on the Peninsula this week, in a grass bowl under oaks that is the nicest outdoor room within an hour of Mountain View. CMAT opens — Irish, very funny, and a far stranger songwriter than the pop framing suggests. Stanford is filed as Peninsula here; it sits just over the Palo Alto line.

events.title: Live the moment light (opens)
events.note: Opens today and runs to 13 December. A group show tracing the influence of Corita Kent — the nun who made silkscreen protest posters out of advertising slogans and was investigated by her own archdiocese for it. Free, as the Art Center always is.

events.title: Palo Alto Philharmonic: Baroque Concert
events.note: Vivaldi and Bach from the volunteer orchestra's baroque ensemble — small forces, which is the right scale for this repertoire. The venue and time were not given in the listing I could reach; check the orchestra's own site before setting out.

events.title: Shawn Mullins
events.note: The man who wrote Lullaby has spent the twenty-five years since writing much better songs to much smaller rooms. Talking-blues delivery, wry, and well suited to a seated 500-seater. Doors 7.

events.title: The Great North Special
events.note: Americana jam band on Broadway in Redwood City. Doors 7. The city's garages are free on Sundays and cheap on Saturday nights, and Caltrain stops three minutes away.

events.title: Summer's End Music Festival
events.note: Six bands, free burgers and face painting in a coastside park, all free. Half Moon Bay is San Mateo County and filed as Peninsula here though the brief does not name it. Highway 92 over the hill backs up badly on a Saturday afternoon — go early, come back late.

events.title: Festa Italiana
events.note: Italian music, dancers, a bocce tournament and a car show, free. South San Francisco is not in the brief's Peninsula list; filed there as the nearest region. Genuinely a community event rather than a heritage-themed food court.

events.title: Rancho Days Fiesta
events.note: Living history at an 1840s adobe on the coast, run by the San Mateo County Historical Association — crafts, demonstrations, and a building most people drive past without noticing. Free. Pacifica is filed as Peninsula here.

events.title: Books and Bunnies: Alan Barillaro and Dashka Slater
events.note: Children's event with Barillaro — the Pixar animator who directed Piper — and Dashka Slater, who writes far harder books for older readers. Time not published in the listing.

events.title: Bark in the Park
events.note: Thirtieth year, and the largest dog festival in the country: roughly 5,000 people and 2,000 dogs in a Naglee Park green. Costume and look-alike contests on the main stage, flyball, adoption row, free vaccines. Free, with a $10 suggested donation that funds the shelters.

events.title: Ice-T and DJ Evil E
events.note: The Rhyme Syndicate pairing that made the records — Ice-T with his original DJ, in a 500-seat university theatre rather than a casino ballroom. Very few tickets were left at the time of writing.

events.title: Elder, Blackwater Holylight
events.note: Elder play long-form heavy psych that left doom behind years ago — closer to prog than to stoner rock now. Blackwater Holylight underneath are the better-kept secret. The strongest bill in downtown San Jose this week.

events.title: Godsmack, Stone Temple Pilots, Dorothy
events.note: Nineteen dollars on the lawn for a 1990s hard-rock triple bill, which is less than a cinema ticket. Stone Temple Pilots are the draw and the caveat — Scott Weiland has been dead a decade and the band carries on without him.

events.title: Moon Festival: Tết Trung Thu
events.note: The Vietnamese mid-autumn festival in East San Jose — lion dancing, lantern parade, food stalls, ten hours of it. San Jose has one of the largest Vietnamese populations outside Vietnam and this is where that shows. Admission was not stated; expect a small door charge.

events.title: Total Vibez Live: Keyshia Cole, Ashanti
events.note: An outdoor R&B festival by the Guadalupe River, early-2000s billing. A companion reggae day, Good Vibez, uses the same field on Sunday. Downtown San Jose parking on a festival Saturday is grim; VTA to Children's Discovery Museum is the move.

events.title: The Authentic & Traditional Garba
events.note: Open-air Gujarati garba — circular folk dance, live singers, and a floor that fills with several hundred people in full dress. Navratri proper is still weeks off, so this is the warm-up. Beginners are genuinely welcome; the steps are repetitive by design.

events.title: Circus Caballero
events.note: A travelling Mexican-tradition circus under a tent in a shopping-centre car park, with multiple shows Thursday to Sunday. Listed once for the run. Milpitas is not named in the brief's region lists; filed as South Bay. Expensive for what it is.

events.title: Jude Berman: The Lie
events.note: A local novelist on Castro Street talking about her tech thriller — the genre Silicon Valley keeps generating and rarely reads. Bookshop events are normally free; time was not listed.

events.title: Haight Ashbury Street Fair
events.note: Forty-seventh year, free, two music stages and more than two hundred vendors across six blocks. It began in 1978 as a merchants' response to the neighbourhood's decline and has outlasted most of what it was responding to. The N-Judah and the 7 will be overwhelmed; walk in through the park.

events.title: Comedy Day in the Park
events.venue: Robin Williams Meadow, Golden Gate Park
events.note: Free, five hours, fifty-plus comedians doing five minutes each in the meadow now named for Robin Williams, who played it repeatedly. Running since 1981 and funded by donations. Bring a blanket and accept that a third of the sets will not land — that is the format.

events.title: Chinatown Autumn Moon Festival (final day)
events.note: Day two. Sunday is the busier of the pair and the day the lion dance troupes work the full length of Grant. It conflicts directly with the Haight fair and with Comedy Day — pick one, all three is a bad afternoon.

events.title: Golden Gate Park Band: Symphony in the Park, Irish Celebration
events.venue: Spreckels Temple of Music, Golden Gate Park
events.note: The 144th season of a municipal band that has played this bandshell since 1882, and one of the last Sundays of the year for it — the season ends with September. An Irish programme this week. Free, donations welcome, and the Music Concourse holds fog past one o'clock.

events.title: LGBTQ+ big band jazz in the AIDS Memorial Grove
events.venue: National AIDS Memorial Grove, Golden Gate Park
events.note: Free, outdoors, in the dell the city set aside as a living memorial. A full big band in a sunken grove of redwoods and fern, two and a half hours. The quietest good thing on a very loud Sunday.

events.title: Fiesta on the Hill
events.note: Thirty-fifth year, run by the Bernal Heights Neighborhood Center: Cortland Avenue closes, the whole hill turns out, and it stays a neighbourhood fair rather than a destination. The smallest and warmest of Sunday's four street festivals.

events.title: San Francisco Armenian Food Festival
events.note: Free on Sunday, $5 on the Friday and Saturday. Church-hall cooking done properly — lahmajoun, kufta, and a pastry table that is the actual reason people drive out to Brotherhood Way for it.

events.title: Japanese Block Party
events.note: Free entry, nine hours, run by a Michelin-starred kaiseki restaurant out onto its own street. Food and drink are paid but the programming is not.

events.title: Lindy in the Park
events.note: Every Sunday since 1997, weather permitting: free swing dancing on the closed stretch of JFK, with a beginners' lesson at the start. Listed once for the window. It is a short walk from Flower Piano's last day, which makes a good afternoon.

events.title: Golden Gate Park Roller Disco
events.note: The Church of 8 Wheels crowd on the old skating slab near 6th Avenue, free, every Sunday. Bring skates or watch — the regulars have been doing this since the 1970s and are worth watching either way.

events.title: Free Shakespeare in the Park
events.note: SF Shakespeare Festival's touring production, free, ninety minutes, on the grass by the Embarcadero. No ticket, no seating — bring something to sit on. The company has done this free every year since 1983.

events.title: Jazz on the Bay Festival
events.note: Outdoor jazz on Treasure Island with the skyline directly across the water. The lineup was not published in the listing I could reach, so this is a venue-and-view recommendation rather than an artist one. Treasure Island is exposed and cold by four.

events.title: LOVE SUPREME day party: Travie Bobbito, King Most, Bella D.
events.note: Sliding scale from free, in The Chapel's back garden from two in the afternoon. King Most is one of the best crate DJs in the city and this is the format that suits him — soul, funk and Latin records in daylight.

events.title: Meltt, Low Hum
events.note: Vancouver dream-pop in the most beautiful music room in the city — 1907 balconies, gilt, frescoed ceiling. Twenty-five dollars to stand under that is the bargain of the week. Doors 7.

events.title: Lane 8
events.note: SOLD OUT, and it is a phones-away set — Lane 8 enforces it, which is either the appeal or the dealbreaker. An early start for a dance show: doors 5, on at 6.

events.title: Built Like Alaska, Talking Ghosts, Poor Image
events.note: A Sunday matinee — doors 3, music 3:30, home by seven. Modesto slowcore with a long, quiet catalogue. Bottom of the Hill's afternoon shows are one of the better ideas in the city and there are not many left before it closes.

events.title: SOLYA, Tele Novella
events.note: Tele Novella underneath are the reason to come: Texan baroque pop built out of harpsichord, harmony and a sense of humour about the whole thing. Doors 7.

events.title: Lauren Sanderson, XKYLAR
events.note: Confessional pop-rap with a devoted queer following, in the basement. Sanderson built the audience herself, entirely outside radio, which is most of what is interesting about her.

events.title: A.CHAL
events.note: Peruvian-American singer working a hazy, narcotic blend of Latin trap and R&B. Door time was not published — The Midway's Sunday shows usually start earlier than its Saturdays.

events.title: Hubba Hubba Revue: 20th Anniversary Superspectacular
events.note: Twenty years of the Bay Area's most committed burlesque and variety troupe, in one anniversary show. Silly, filthy, extremely well-drilled, and a genuine institution of the DNA's upstairs room. 18+.

events.title: BIIRD (night 2)
events.note: Second of two nights. Friday sold out; this one had not at the time of writing. Doors 7.

events.title: Sundays at the Beach: tai chi on the Great Highway
events.note: Free open-air tai chi on the promenade now permanently closed to cars, facing the ocean. Turn up, no registration. The fog usually burns off the beach around eleven, which is after you finish.

events.title: Berkeley Jam: juggling and circus arts festival
events.note: Second year, free, all ages: workshops, skill shares, open jams and — the detail that makes it — a homemade jam tasting contest, because of the name. Six hours in a park off Telegraph. The best pure oddity of the week.

events.title: Blues, Brews & BBQ
events.note: Ninth year, free, six hours of live blues in an Alameda park by the beach. RSVP only if you want the prize drawings. One of the few festivals this weekend where you can park without a plan.

events.title: portrayal of guilt, Loma Prieta, NØ MAN
events.note: Three bands of genuinely extreme screamo and blackened hardcore in a 150-person room, with San Jose's own Loma Prieta in the middle. It will be unbearably loud and that is the specification, not a complaint.

events.title: Spotlight Sundays: Alice Street screening with Malonga Arts
events.note: The documentary about the fight to save the Alice Street mural — a block from the museum — with live dance and drumming from the Malonga Center company whose community the film is about. Ten dollars, and the pairing is the point.

events.title: Radiator Hospital
events.note: Sam Cook-Parrott's band: short, fast, bruised power-pop songs about being wrong about someone. Fifteen years of records that nobody outside the basement-show circuit ever quite noticed.

events.title: Dirty Cello, Rockbusters
events.note: Cello played like a blues guitar, in a West Berkeley taproom. Usually free at this venue, but the listing did not say — assume a tip bucket.

events.title: Rob Zombie, Marilyn Manson, Orgy, The HU
events.note: A 1990s shock-rock package tour. The HU, the Mongolian throat-singing metal band opening, are by a distance the most interesting thing on the bill and will play to a half-empty lawn. BART Concord plus a shuttle, about twenty minutes.

events.title: Alameda Legacy Home Tour: Fernside storybook houses
events.note: Inside half a dozen 1920s and 30s Storybook-style houses — the deliberately crooked, fairy-tale revival style that Alameda has more of than anywhere else in the region. Self-guided, six hours, forty dollars.

events.title: The Liver
events.venue: Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: A Korean-language musical touring into Castro Street's main house for a single performance. Whether it is surtitled was not stated anywhere I could reach — worth a call to the box office if you do not read Korean.

events.title: Good Vibez Live
events.note: Reggae-rock day on the same downtown field that hosts Saturday's R&B bill — two festivals, one meadow, one weekend. Lineup and price were not published in the listings I could reach.

events.title: Charles Hood: Acorns in a Nutshell
events.note: A poet and naturalist on the oak — a whole book about acorns, which in California is a book about almost everything else too. Time not published.

events.title: The Texas Headhunters
events.note: Texas blues-rock, third Guild booking of the weekend — the room is running a full Wednesday-to-Sunday week, which is unusual for the Peninsula and worth encouraging. Doors 7.
